tasks.title: Onboarding Wave 1: basic info with optional alias and upload invitation
tasks.outcome: Wave 1 becomes a fixed, friendly onboarding form with 7-8 low-stakes questions. Users may use an alias/fake name, share city and living situation, current role and education, and are invited—but not required—to upload a resume, MBTI or other supporting material at the end.
done_when: lib/interview/templates.ts defines 7-8 simple info questions with single_choice, multi_choice and short_text; every question allows skip and custom input; name question explicitly says an alias is OK.
buildWave1Canonical maps the new questions to elicitation units, target dimensions and provenance without breaking the Wave runtime contract.
The Wave 1 sensemaker prompt (lib/ai/sensemaker/wave.ts) is light: it acknowledges the basic facts, repeats the user's stated constraints, and avoids deep interpretation or clinical labels.
The post-Wave 1 UI (app/play/page.tsx or InsightSlip) shows a soft, optional upload invitation for resume / MBTI / other, and the existing upload consent and UploadPanel remain usable.
Existing integration tests that reference w1q1-w1q4 are updated, or a compatibility shim keeps old answer shapes from failing.
pnpm typecheck, build, lint, test:contracts and test:e2e all pass.
boundaries: No profiling, scoring, or hidden questionnaire logic.
Do not require real name, phone, ID or any high-sensitivity PII.
Upload remains optional and gated by the existing upload consent.
Wave 1 stays a fixed template; no AI interviewer call for Wave 1.

progress.next: Update Wave 1 template and sensemaker prompt

tasks.title: Async Final Plan delivery by email and shareable token link
tasks.outcome: When the user reaches the plan/Odyssey stage, the app jumps to a dedicated email-collection screen, immediately acknowledges submission, runs Final Plan generation in the background, and sends the user an email with a secure, opaque link to view the report on a standalone /report/[token] page.
done_when: The stop step in app/play/page.tsx (and/or app/plan/page.tsx) collects an email, validates it, and submits to POST /api/final.
POST /api/final accepts an optional email, returns 202 immediately, and uses next/after (or an equivalent background continuation) to call runSensemakerFinal without blocking the HTTP response.
The generated FinalPlan is persisted with a new report_token; if a plan already exists for the session, the existing token is returned instead of regenerating.
A new lib/mail/ module provides a configurable mailer with a local dev fallback (console/transporter via env SMTP) and a sendReportLink(email, token, url) helper.
A new app/report/[token]/page.tsx route renders the FinalPlan from the token; it does not require a cookie or login.
The report email contains a Chinese subject, a short message, and a link like https://<host>/report/<token>.
Token lookup is idempotent and 404s cleanly for unknown tokens.
Integration and contract tests cover: email collection, async final, report token access, missing token 404, and idempotent final.
pnpm typecheck, build, lint, test:contracts and test:e2e all pass.
boundaries: Do not build a full user-account or password system; token link is the first version.
Do not store email as searchable user identity; store it only as the delivery address for the report (hashed if possible without breaking email resend).
Do not expose session secret or guest-token in the email link.
Keep the report page read-only and shareable: the recipient can view but not mutate the plan.

progress.next: Add email collection and report token flow
